 9-1-1: Nashville crossover: what's confirmed, when it airs, and which Lone Star faces are in play
 9-1-1: Nashville crossover: what's confirmed, when it airs, and which Lone Star faces are in play
 by
 Hannah Whitlock 
 Nov 19, 2026 2:49 pm 
 ✓ Verified by editorial team 
 Image credit: Legion Media 
 The 118 is coming back to Music City, and Maddie is already on set. Whether the 126 joins them is the question Lone Star fans have been asking for almost two years.
 Here's where things stand as of mid-November: a big 9-1-1 crossover is coming to 9-1-1: Nashville season 2, it's already filming, and ABC still hasn't announced an airdate. Lone Star characters are officially "in the works," and nobody has been officially cast yet.
 What's confirmed
 Showrunner Rashad Raisani, who also ran 9-1-1: Lone Star , laid out the season 2 plan to TVLine before the October 15 premiere. There would be two crossovers: a small one early in the season and a much bigger one later.
 The small one already happened. In episode 2, "Boys and Boils," the 113 got a call about a baby crying inside a wall, a callback to the very first episode of 9-1-1 , and Ryan called Buck and Chimney for advice. Raisani's description: "a fun thing where [the 118] help us solve a problem."
 Members of the 118 in 9-1-1 (2018). The original 9-1-1 is set to cross over with Nashville again in the spinoff's second season. Image credit: Legion Media The big one is the event:
 "We also want to do another big OG crossover. And I've been saying from day one that I want to bring some 'Lone Star' people in, and that's in the works in a big way. I think that'll be a really great crossover around Episode 8 or 9."
 — Rashad Raisani, showrunner, to TVLine
 The first on-set proof arrived on November 11. Jennifer Love Hewitt posted a video with Ryan Phillippe, both in costume, with the caption "@ryanphillippe I loved seeing you again." That's Maddie from 9-1-1 sharing a set with Nashville 's Phillippe, and an I Know What You Did Last Summer reunion 29 years in the making.
 When does it air?
 ABC hasn't said. Here's the math in the meantime:
 Episode 6 , "Tears of the Nile," airs this Thursday, November 19.
 Episodes 8 and 9 , Raisani's target window, land after that. With Thanksgiving week and the usual holiday break, that points to December at the earliest and possibly early 2027.
 Season 2 has 18 episodes ordered, so there's room to move it.
 One thing to know before you plan your night: last season's "two-hour crossover event" was more lopsided than the promo suggested. The 9-1-1 half aired first, but none of the Nashville characters actually appeared in it. Buck and Eddie did all the traveling.
 Don't miss: How to watch 9-1-1 in order before you start season 10 or Nashville season 2 
 Which Lone Star faces are in play
 Nobody from Lone Star has been announced. But Raisani has been unusually specific about who he wants, and some of the candidates have been campaigning in public.
 T.K. and Carlos (Ronen Rubinstein and Rafael Silva). Raisani's top priority from the start. He even pitched how it would work: "Carlos coming in as a Texas Ranger and TK with him just visiting town because Carlos is consulting on a case." In his TVLine interview, he dropped another hint: "There was a certain paramedic from New York from the show that Roxie might know." T.K. was a paramedic from New York.
 Owen Strand (Rob Lowe). Lone Star 's finale left Owen alive and working as New York's fire chief, and Lowe has never hidden that he'd come back. He has a family connection, too: his brother Chad Lowe directs and executive produces Nashville . "I hired him on Lone Star . I think turnabout is fair play," Lowe told Decider. He's since told TV Insider he has a specific pitch, with one condition: "They would have to woo me."
 That's two strong candidates, one showrunner who wants them, and zero signed contracts.
 Every 9-1-1 show eventually learns the same lesson: the fastest way to start a fire is to promise fans T.K. and Carlos and then not say when.
 There's one practical complication. Rubinstein now has a new day job as Jude Callan on Starz's S.W.A.T. Exiles , whose first season wraps on November 27. He's said he'd love to know how T.K. is "doing as a stay-at-home dad," but his schedule is a real factor in whether that happens this season.
 The bottom line
 Here's what you can count on: the original 9-1-1 is coming back to Nashville this season, Maddie is involved, and the plan is for it to land around episodes 8 or 9. Here's what's still a wish list: anyone from Austin.
 Raisani has said "that's in the works in a big way," and he's the one person who has run both shows. Until ABC sends out a press release with Rubinstein's or Silva's name on it, though, Lone Star fans should keep their expectations on simmer, not boil.
